rules.what: a script that runs at install time (preinstall, postinstall, setup.py install override, a .pth file)
rules.why: 2 for any hook, 3 when it runs js, 5 when it downloads something or is a .pth; husky, node-gyp and the like count 1

rules.what: eval over decoded data, strings built char by char, long hex runs, base64 that decodes to code, python exec over decoded bytes
rules.why: minified vendor bundles are skipped for shape, not for content; images, fonts and wasm in base64 do not count

rules.what: reads secret files (.ssh, .npmrc, .aws, wallets, browser stores) and sends somewhere in the same package
rules.why: 5 when both halves are there, 4 for a webhook or collaborator domain alone, 3 for env + secret paths + network in one file, 1 for a raw ip or throwaway domain alone

rules.what: a hardcoded address next to clipboard access (a clipper), or code that reaches into wallet / browser credential storage
rules.why: two storage markers, or one marker plus wallet words plus a network call; never from comment lines

rules.what: reverse shell shapes, download-and-run one-liners, persistence (cron, rc files, startup) next to a shell call
rules.why: chmod +x && ./run counts 3; a scanner's own pattern lists and comments are skipped

rules.what: windows executables, MZ or ELF files shipped with an install hook and no native build declared
rules.why: a python package carrying an .exe with no hook counts 2

rules.what: a new name one keystroke, one swap or one suffix away from a popular one
rules.why: popular lists come from the registries themselves; established packages are exempt

established: first release over a year ago, or over 50k weekly downloads: heuristics alone never put it on the wall
never: names a package without the lines that tripped
calls anything confirmed without a public advisory
